extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys handling appeals to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedures and required actions following Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences decisions, including requests for rehearing, amendments or showings of facts, examiner/Board interplay, reopening prosecution, withdrawals/dismissals, and judicial review timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after Board new 37 CFR 1.196(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board makes a new rejection under 37 CFR 1.196(b), the appellant has the option of (A) requesting rehearing or (B) submitting an appropriate amendment of the rejected claims, and/or a showing of facts relating to the claims so rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appellant submits an amendment and/or showing, the application is remanded to the examiner. The new ground of rejection is binding on the examiner unless an amendment or showing of facts not previously of record overcomes it. If the examiner again rejects the claims, appellant may appeal again under §§ 1.191–1.195 to the Board. A request for rehearing must address the new ground and state with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked; the Board will rehear the new ground and, if necessary, render a new decision including all grounds upon which a patent is refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to reject allowed claims (37 CFR 1.196(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.196(b), the Board may, in its decision, make a new rejection of one or more of any of the claims pending in the case, including claims which have been allowed by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authorization is discretionary and not an instruction to reexamine every allowed claim; no inference should be drawn from a failure to exercise that discretion. See MPEP § 1214.01 for procedure following a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and availability of Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Board may be published at the discretion of the Commissioner; public decisions are made available electronically on the PTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to publish a decision should be referred to the Office of the Solicitor. A decision in a pending or abandoned application will be published in accordance with 37 CFR 1.14(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Action following Board decision (37 CFR 1.197(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, the application will be returned to the examiner for such further action by appellant or examiner as the condition of the application may require to carry into effect the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must take appropriate action depending on whether rejections are reversed, affirmed, or a new ground was entered (see MPEP §§ 1214.01–1214.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing requirements (37 CFR 1.197(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing must be filed within two months from the date of the original decision and must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked and all other grounds upon which rehearing is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'rehearing' refers to rehearing on the written record, not entitlement to an oral hearing. Many requests are mere reargument; the rule limits requests to points of law or fact believed to have been overlooked or misapprehended. See § 1.136(b) and § 1.550(c) for extension rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-extension limits for rehearing and responses (37 CFR 1.196(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Time periods for requesting rehearing of the Board's new rejection under 37 CFR 1.196(b), or for submitting an amendment or showing of facts, may not be extended by filing a petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are available only under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or under 37 CFR 1.550(c) if the appeal involves a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment or showing of facts after 1.196(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant elects to proceed before the examiner, he or she must submit an appropriate amendment of the claims so rejected or a showing of facts relating to the claims so rejected, or both, within the 2-month period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An argument without amendment or showing of facts can result only in a final rejection since the examiner cannot allow the claims unless amended or the rejection is overcome by a showing of facts not before the Board. Amended or new claims must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims. An appellant's request for rehearing accompanied by an affidavit adding facts does not afford rehearing as a matter of right under 1.196(b); the Board may remand to the examiner, and the examiner may withdraw the Board's rejection based on the affidavit and remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of proceeding (rehearing) on right to further prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rehearing by the Board must be filed within 2 months; 'By proceeding in this manner, the appellant waives his or her right to further prosecution before the examiner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board's decision includes an affirmance of the examiner's rejection, a rehearing of the affirmance should be filed in a separate paper to facilitate consideration. Context-specific: the quoted waiver appears in the discussion of requests for rehearing and relates to procedural consequences of choosing rehearing pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner conduct after Board reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner's rejection is completely reversed by the Board, the examiner should take appropriate action but should never regard such a reversal as a challenge to make a new search to uncover other and better references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second examiner should give full faith and credit to the prior examiner's search. If the examiner has specific knowledge of particular references indicating non-patentability, submit the matter to the Group Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198 for the purpose of entering the new rejection; Group Director's approval is placed on the action reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner request for rehearing of Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may request rehearing of the Board decision; such a request should normally be made within 2 months of receipt of the Board decision in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests must be approved by the Group Director and forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Patent Policy and Projects for approval before mailing. The request should set a period of 1 month for the appellant to file a reply; after the reply period (plus mailing time) has expired, the file will be forwarded to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of withdrawn claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appellant withdraws some of the appealed claims, and the Board reverses the examiner on the remaining appealed claims, the withdrawal is treated as an authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims; it is not necessary to notify the appellant of the cancellation of the withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A withdrawal of the appeal as to some claims operates as authorization to cancel those claims; the withdrawn claims will be canceled by direction of the examiner at the conclusion of the appeal proceedings if necessary, without further action by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings and abandonment when no claims allowed (37 CFR 1.197(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are considered terminated by dismissal of an appeal or failure to timely file an appeal to the court or a civil action, except where claims stand allowed or further action by the examiner is required; if no claims stand allowed the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of termination is the date the appeal is dismissed or the time for court action expires. The time for seeking review by the Federal Circuit or District of Columbia is the same (2 months) and when that time has passed without review, the examiner must take up the application. If proceedings terminate and no claims are allowed, stamp abandoned and send to abandoned files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims when parent claim rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim is affirmed/rejected and dependent claims were objected to as allowable except for dependency, the examiner should either (1) convert the dependent claim into independent form by examiner's amendment, cancel all claims in which the rejection was affirmed, and issue the application; or (2) set a 1-month time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted for the 1-month period. If no timely reply is received, the examiner will cancel rejected and objected-to claims and issue the application with the allowed claims only. Suggested form language and examiner notes are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims standing allowed — examiner action and formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims stand allowed after Board decision, the appellant is not required to file a reply; the examiner passes the application to issue on the claims which stand allowed and marks the file accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncorrected formal matters remain that cannot be handled without written correspondence, the examiner should take appropriate action but prosecution is otherwise closed. A shortened statutory period (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) may be set to correct formal matters; extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136 for such formal corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after Board decision (37 CFR 1.198) — petition standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases decided by the Board will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under provisions of § 1.196, without written authority of the Commissioner, and then only for consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments filed after the Board's decision do not entitle appellant to have them entered as a matter of right. If an amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance, the primary examiner should recommend entry and, with concurrence of the Supervisory Patent Examiner, the amendment will be entered. If not entered, the examiner should write stating the reason; refusal should not appear arbitrary. Petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen prosecution are decided by the Group Director; such petitions will ordinarily be granted only in limited categories (see guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories warranting petitions to reopen under 37 CFR 1.198
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to reopen will ordinarily be granted only when: (A) Board decision suggests a curable defect such that amended claims would be allowable; (B) Board decision asserts the record lacks evidence of a specified character and such evidence exists or could be presented; or (C) Board decision is based on a practice, rule, or judicial precedent which since the decision has been rescinded, repealed, or overruled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions will not ordinarily be entertained after the filing of the Commissioner's brief in 35 U.S.C. 141 cases or after trial in 35 U.S.C. 145 cases. If a petition in a 141 appeal is granted, steps are taken to request the court to remand the case so proposed amendments/evidence/arguments can be entered of record for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal — effects and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney not of record may file a paper withdrawing an appeal except where withdrawal would result in abandonment; withdrawal after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired results in abandonment unless there are allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter abandoning the application under 37 CFR 1.138 has an effective date of abandonment equal to recognition by an appropriate official of the Office or another date specified in the letter. If a brief has been filed within time and an answer mailed and appellant withdraws, the application is returned to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial withdrawal of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of the appeal as to some of the claims on appeal operates as an authorization to cancel those claims from the application; the appeal continues as to the remaining claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The withdrawn claims will be canceled from the application by direction of the examiner at the conclusion of the appeal proceedings, if necessary, without further action by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeal for failure to file brief (37 CFR 1.192)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed, the appeal stands dismissed; if no claims stand allowed the application is considered abandoned as of the date the brief was due. If claims stand allowed, dismissal is treated as withdrawal of the appeal and of any claim not standing allowed; the application should be passed to issue forthwith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-461 or form paragraph 12.17 may be used to notify the appellant that the appeal stands dismissed; such a notification is not an action in the case and does not start any period for reply. The appeal should not be dismissed until any extended period (e.g., 5 months under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file the brief has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for seeking judicial review (35 U.S.C. 141 and 145)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for seeking review of a Board decision by the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia is 2 months (or 2 months with the extension provided by 37 CFR 1.304 if a request for rehearing is timely filed before the Board), unless otherwise extended by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal to the Federal Circuit waives the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145. Procedures and effects of appeals under 35 U.S.C. 141, 145, and 146 are described, including remand and the effect on evidence and costs in civil actions.
